messages:
emily.docs: FYI PR #2521 uncovered an inconsistency for files.upload examples. The docs show `metadata` as an object in the multipart examples, but the runtime expects the `metadata` form field to be a JSON string.

emily.docs: In practice Node SDK automagically stringifies objects in multipart form-data, so examples using raw objects looked fine in node but break for strongly typed SDKs (Go/Rust) and direct curl users. Need a small docs + spec fix.

rachel-sdk: Got it. Which example specifically? Can you paste the curl that failed?

emily.docs: Sure — current docs example: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files/upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F "file=@./report.pdf" \
  -F "metadata={\"title\":\"Q1 report\",\"team\":\"sales\"}"
```
This example works in Node because the browser/node multipart helper ends up sending metadata as a string. But our OpenAPI example (and one of the curl snippets) rendered metadata without quotes around keys which is ambiguous for curl users.

jon.runtime: Confirming runtime: we parse metadata as a JSON string. We accept both string and empty/missing; we don't accept a raw multipart object. If the incoming part is not valid JSON string, we return 422.

rachel-sdk: Go SDK's FilesUpload helper currently builds multipart parts from map[string]interface{} and encodes object parts as raw bytes (no JSON string) which triggers runtime 422. Node/Python higher-level libs often stringify implicitly, so they passed.

mark.api: Action: we should update the OpenAPI examples to show metadata as an explicit JSON string in multipart examples and add a short note: "metadata must be a JSON-encoded string". Also update the SDKs: Go SDK should JSON.Marshal metadata parts; add a compatibility note in docs.

emily.docs: I'll update the docs examples (curl/node/py) and add a migration snippet explaining curl escaping for linux/mac/windows. Will also add a short troubleshooting FAQ entry for 422 errors from files.upload.

rachel-sdk: I'll open a Go SDK PR to JSON-encode metadata parts in FilesUpload and add a unit test that posts a map and verifies server accepts it. ETA: 4h. I'll bump the changelog and include a note about breaking behavior for clients that assumed object parts are allowed.

jon.runtime: I'll add an explicit example in the OpenAPI spec showing the multipart boundary with metadata as a JSON string and include a sample server response for invalid (422) vs valid (200).

ci-bot: CI: docs PR #2521 lint OK, integration tests: files-upload/CurlExamples failing on windows-escaping test 01. See https://ci.internal/rdw/2521/job/77 (log).

mark.api: Plan: 1) @jon.runtime update OpenAPI + example payload 2) @rachel-sdk open Go PR to JSON-encode metadata parts 3) @emily.docs patch docs + FAQ + platform-specific curl escapes 4) QA: run manual curl and SDK smoke tests post-merge. Target: tomorrow AM.

emily.docs: I'll add a tiny "How to submit metadata via curl" subsection showing the exact escaping for bash/powershell so folks don't hit the CI windows issue.

rachel-sdk: Leaving a note in the Go PR: maintainers who pass already-stringified JSON should not double-encode; helper will detect string vs object and only marshal objects.

mark.api: Thanks all, ping me when PRs are up and I'll coordinate a short batch merge to avoid docs/runtime drift.
